sentences.en: Nakajima does not hide his interest in the family situation of a man named Takakura Yutaro. Whether he is single or married is the only option, but he is too scared to ask him directly, so instead, he is probing his classmate Kumai for information. Just as the conversation was about to delve into personal matters, Sanako quietly interjected and redirected the discussion back to the issue of cash payments for the advance payment. sentences.en: Yutaro Takakura finally made it to the office. He spotted his old friend Kumai and, unusually for him, almost broke into a smile, but that expression tightened the moment he heard Nakajima from the sales department. Upon learning that Kumai had handled the accounting without Yutaro, he took a small step back, interrupting Mayu's words as she seemed about to speak, and led Kumai out toward the hallway. The gesture alone conveyed that there was something they wanted to discuss privately. As Sanako watched the whole exchange, she felt a small sense of unease lingering in her heart. The long-standing friendship since high school, Kumai's gesture of trying to take on the accounting responsibilities, and the numerous overlapping records of advances all suggested that there was something between those two that she was unaware of.

sentences.en: At the end of the hallway, the two of them were quietly laughing together for a while. It seemed like a lighthearted conversation between old friends, but beneath that laughter lay an intimacy shared only by those who had something they couldn't show to others. When Kumai brought up the topic of the expenses to be reimbursed, Yutaro somewhat forcefully tried to take it over. He casually attempted to skip the usual steps of confirming the date and endorsements, which were natural procedures for someone in charge of accounting. Even when Sanako raised her voice, he brushed her off with a simple, "I'll be right back." Sanako thought it was unlike him. For the first time, she felt as if she had touched on a shadow of a senior colleague she had worked with for many years that had remained unseen.

sentences.en: Some time later, on a certain afternoon, Yamada Taiyou found Sanako in the company hallway. He was about to start a conversation with his usual carefree smile, making excuses that he was just stopping by as part of his sales work, when in reality, he had come just to see her. It seemed he wanted to talk about the ramen they all had eaten together recently, but his phrasing was oddly familiar, potentially leading to misunderstandings for anyone listening. Sanako was still unaccustomed to this kind of closeness. She extremely disliked the idea of personal exchanges mixing with someone else's ears. For that reason, she felt a strong desire to keep their relationship strictly professional. However, it was unclear whether Yamada was aware of the height of her walls or not.

Advances, contract renewals, Kumai's documents, Yuu's attitude. She felt each fact drawing closer to forming a single picture. Even the sight of the noisy Kamamoto in front of her felt somewhat distant. Mayu hurried over and checked Kamamoto's arm, which was heated. Sanako quietly stood up and moved away from the scene.

The only voice echoing in her mind was Yuu's low voice, repeating, "In the end, everything gets settled." Even though that one phrase made sense within Yuu's logic, it didn't hold up within the framework of accounting. Squinting, Sanako followed the data. The division of April felt like more than just a change of fiscal year. Kumai's advances had stopped precisely that month, as if something else had rendered them unnecessary.

sentences.en: As she delved into the details of the contract, the increase in the lease fee and the existence of a rebate processed behind the scenes came to light. An increase of two hundred thousand yen, from two million seven hundred thousand yen to two million nine hundred thousand yen. At first glance, this amount could be explained within the context of the economic situation, but when the promise of a five percent rebate is mixed in, the nature of the discussion changes. On the surface, it's a price hike, but in reality, it's close to the original level—if that were to imply someone's influence at play. Sanako's gaze lingered for a moment on the word "rebate."

sentences.en: As Sanako flipped through the documents in front of her, Mayu quietly peered in from behind. It seemed to be the first time she had heard the term "rebate," and she straightforwardly asked for an explanation. In her usual calm voice, Sanako rephrased it in simpler terms: it was a system where the seller, wanting to make their sales appear higher, would not lower the price but would later return a portion of it. Mayu took notes, impressed, as she gradually deepened her understanding of the complexities of accounting. For Sanako, it was important to leave clear words for this junior colleague.

sentences.en: Kumai, who had just returned from shopping, met his wife, Chika, in the hallway. The sight of his wife going out of her way to deliver a homemade bento was exactly the family image he had repeatedly described. Sanako lightly bowed to the two of them from a short distance away. Caught between suspicions about work and the warm scene before her, she struggled to switch her emotions effectively. The more she heard about Kumai's family, the more the stark contrast with the flow of money moving behind the scenes became apparent. Still, when faced with the concept of family, it was human nature not to want to voice a conclusion too easily. Sanako adjusted the documents she was holding against her chest.

sentences.en: Kumai happily introduced his wife, Chika, to Sanako. The conversation quickly turned to the fact that Chika was also a junior at the same high school as Takurayuta. The old story about being the manager of the rugby team shed light on a surprising side of Yuu. Having lost his father at a young age and bearing the weight of his mother's health issues and debts, he managed to graduate from university while also paying for his sister's tuition — this image of Yuu as a hardworking person quietly rewrote Sanako's perception of him. Chika's words, that he was a man without any faults from an outsider's perspective, carried a respect that was not laced with sarcasm. As Sanako listened in silence, she questioned herself again about what she was trying to doubt.
